key_insight: A compact pediatric foundation model (TEDDY) can learn from ICD-coded histories to forecast disease risk and visit timing across a wide range of childhood conditions.
clinical_relevance: This approach could help flag higher-risk children earlier, including rare diseases and common diagnoses like asthma and ADHD, by leveraging routine EHR data.
method: Trained a 1.84M-parameter decoder transformer on ~73 million ICD-10 diagnoses from 1.6 million children.
Modeled both longitudinal diagnosis trajectories and visit timing using first-occurrence prediction tasks.
Compared performance against age- and sex-matched controls and multiple baseline models, including dense, CNN, RNN, LSTM, and a much larger language model.
evidence_signal: Across 797 disease-onset prediction tasks in 16 ICD-10 chapters, TEDDY reached a median AUC of 72.0% and outperformed baselines on 96-99% of tasks, with signal detectable more than two years before diagnosis.
watch_item: Results come from a single pediatric institution, and visit-timing predictions were less well calibrated for median and long-tail return intervals, so external validation is needed before deployment.
paper_title: TEDDY: A Pediatric Foundation Model for Risk Forewarning from ICD-Coded Diagnostic Histories
